t: You're on D'Arblay Street, in Soho. It was once called Portland Street, and was built on land owned by the Dukes of Portland, known as Doghouse Close. The name today honours Frances Burney, the novelist, diarist and playwright, who became Madame d'Arblay when she married the French exile General Alexandre d'Arblay in 1793. She was a celebrated author, best known for her first novel, Evelina, and she served as Keeper of the Robes to Queen Charlotte.
